subject: You know Proverbs. Have you studied it?
preview: Knowing a few verses is not the same as knowing the book.
linkText: Join the Wisdom of Proverbs study

blocks.text: You already know something from Proverbs.
Even if you have never sat down and read it.
"Trust in the LORD with all thine heart."
"Iron sharpeneth iron."
"Train up a child in the way he should go."
You have seen them on coffee mugs, church signs, and somebody's Facebook post.
Maybe you have highlighted a few yourself.
But when was the last time you actually studied Proverbs?
Not a verse. The book.
Most of us use Proverbs like a drawer of loose advice.
We open it when we need something, grab one line, and close it again.
Knowing a few Proverbs is not the same as knowing Proverbs.
Here is something most people miss.
Proverbs does not open with a list of sayings. It opens with a father talking to his son.
For nine chapters he pleads with him. Listen to me. Pay attention. Do not walk down that road.
The short sayings everybody quotes do not even start until chapter 10.
Read those sayings on their own, and they sound like tips.
Read them after the first nine chapters, and they sound like a father who does not want to lose his child.
That changes how every single verse lands.
And it is the kind of thing you only see when you walk through the whole book.
So here is what we are doing in October.
October has 31 days. Proverbs has 31 chapters.
Starting October 1, we are going through Proverbs together inside Bible Buddy. One chapter a day.
Each day has a short lesson, the chapter itself, a few questions, and a conversation with everyone else reading that same chapter.
Instead of collecting Proverbs for another year, spend one month actually understanding the book.
